newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials end firmer but mkt seen quiet.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials end firmer but mkt seen quiet.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares ended firmer in active trade on Monday but brokers said they expected the market to quieten down this week as players looked towards new listings
The key industrial index jumped 80.81 points to close at 10,147.39, lifted largely by gains in several major counters.
"Everything is going very quiet because of the new listings," one broker said.

Manufacturing and construction company Randalls, which made its debut on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Monday, came under a bit of pressure ahead of the closure on Wedensday of merchant banker NMB's issue, he said.
"We believe the NMB issue is drawing out the speculators in Randalls, creating a buying opportunity in the market," another broker said.
Randalls was listed at an opening price of 142 cents with buyers at 140 cents, sellers at 145 cents and deals at 142 followed at 145 cents as 2.4 million shares changed hands.

Among the day's winners, plastics and construction investor IHL leapt 200 cents to 2,200 while publishers Zimpapers at 4,800, hotel and supermarket group Meikles at 2,600, pharmaceutical company Caps at 1,400 and tobacco firm BAT at 1,700 all jumped 100 cents.
Against the tend, bankers Barclays dropped 100 cents to 3,200, finance house UDC lost 20 cents to 320 and horticulture company Ariston shed 15 cents to 215.

The mining board drew little trading as lower metal prices continued to affect sentiment. Gold producers Falgold eased two cents to 68 and Ashanti slid 500 cents to 9,500, pulling the mining index 2.87 points lower to 969.34.
